paragraphs.paragraph: The psalm presents the king’s joy in the LORD’s salvation, the granting of his heart’s desires and prayers, and the blessings, life, honor, majesty, and joy God gives him.
paragraphs.title: The King’s Joy and Blessings

easy.explanation: The king greatly rejoices in the LORD’s salvation.
easy.q: In what does the king rejoice?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou hast given him his heart’s desire.”
easy.q: What did God give the king?

easy.explanation: The LORD set a crown of pure gold on his head.
easy.q: What was set upon the king’s head?

answers: His heart’s desire and the request of his lips
medium.explanation: The passage says God gave him his heart’s desire and the request of his lips.
medium.q: What two things did the king ask for and receive from God?

answers: A request or prayer spoken by the king
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the king’s spoken request before God.
medium.q: What does “the request of his lips” refer to?

answers: Blessings, life, honor, majesty, and joy
medium.explanation: The verses mention blessings, long life, glory, honor, majesty, and gladness.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the blessings given to the king?

answers: The salvation is the source of his great rejoicing
The salvation causes him to fear
The salvation has no connection with his joy
challenge.explanation: The king rejoices greatly in the LORD’s salvation.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s salvation and the king’s joy?

answers: That the king’s life is brief
That the king receives enduring and abundant life
That life depends on the king’s wealth
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes an exceedingly long and continuing life.
challenge.q: What do the words “length of days for ever and ever” emphasize?

answers: The king receives abundant blessing from the LORD
The king must fight without help
The king gives up his joy
challenge.explanation: The passage describes life, glory, honor, majesty, blessing, and joy from God.
challenge.q: Which idea includes most of the gifts described in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: The psalm presents the king’s joy in the LORD’s salvation, the granting of his heart’s desires and prayers, and the blessings, life, honor, majesty, and joy God gives him.

paragraphs.paragraph: The king trusts in the LORD, and through the mercy of the most High he remains secure and is not moved.
paragraphs.title: The King’s Trust in God

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the king trusteth in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does the king trust?

answers: Through the mercy of the most High
easy.explanation: His stability is connected with the mercy of the most High.
easy.q: Through what will the king not be moved?

easy.explanation: The verse says that he “shall not be moved.”
easy.q: What is the king’s condition according to the verse?

answers: His trust in the LORD is connected with his not being moved
His trust causes him to leave the LORD
The verse gives no connection between them
medium.explanation: The verse joins the king’s trust in the LORD with his secure condition.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the king’s trust and his stability?

answers: He will not fall or be shaken
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the king will remain firm and secure.
medium.q: What does “shall not be moved” mean in this verse?

answers: As the most High, whose mercy gives security
medium.explanation: The verse refers to “the mercy of the most High.”
medium.q: How is God described in this verse?

challenge.explanation: The verse specifically states that the king trusts in the LORD.
challenge.q: What central quality of the king is emphasized?

answers: Trust in the LORD gives him stability and security
Trust causes him to turn away from God
challenge.explanation: The verse connects confidence in God with remaining firm.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the words “trusteth” and “shall not be moved”?

answers: The mercy of the most High
challenge.explanation: The king shall not be moved through the mercy of the most High.
challenge.q: What is the foundation of the king’s stability?

paragraphs.idea: The king trusts in the LORD, and through the mercy of the most High he remains secure and is not moved.

paragraphs.paragraph: The poet describes the king’s reach against his enemies and their destruction by God, after their evil plans cannot be carried out.
paragraphs.title: Victory over the Enemies

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thine hand shall find out all thine enemies.”
easy.q: Whom shall the king’s hand find?

easy.explanation: The passage describes the enemies being consumed and destroyed.
easy.q: What will happen to the enemies?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “They intended evil against thee.”

answers: They have no time to act
God will overcome and destroy them
The king will abandon the battle
medium.explanation: The passage describes the LORD swallowing them up and preventing their plans.
medium.q: Why will the enemies’ evil plans fail?

medium.explanation: It refers to the evil plan the enemies imagined.
medium.q: What does “a mischievous device” mean in this passage?

answers: The enemies plan evil, but God destroys them
The king is defeated, and the enemies praise him
The enemies bless the king, and he flees
medium.explanation: The enemies devise evil, but the LORD brings judgment upon them.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the passage?

answers: The intensity of their judgment and destruction
challenge.explanation: The image conveys severe and consuming judgment.
challenge.q: What does the image of “a fiery oven” emphasize about the enemies’ fate?

answers: They plan evil, but the LORD prevents their plan from succeeding
Their plan succeeds, and they are rescued
challenge.explanation: The verse says they imagined an evil device which they were not able to perform.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the enemies’ intended evil and their inability to perform it?

answers: The LORD’s action against the enemies
challenge.explanation: The LORD is the one who swallows up and destroys the enemies.
challenge.q: What is the source of the victory described in this passage?

paragraphs.idea: The poet describes the king’s reach against his enemies and their destruction by God, after their evil plans cannot be carried out.

paragraphs.paragraph: At the end of the psalm, the poet asks the LORD to be exalted in His strength so that all may sing and praise His power.
paragraphs.title: Praise for God’s Might

answers: To be exalted in His strength
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength.”
easy.q: What does the poet ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “so will we sing and praise thy power.”
easy.q: What will they do in response?

easy.explanation: They will sing and praise the LORD’s power.
easy.q: What is the subject of their song?

answers: Be lifted up and shown in greatness
medium.explanation: The request is for the LORD to be exalted and revealed in His strength.
medium.q: What does “Be thou exalted” mean in this verse?

answers: The display of His strength leads them to sing and praise
Their song is intended only for the enemies
medium.explanation: The verse connects God’s exaltation with their singing and praise.
medium.q: What is the relationship between God’s strength and their singing?

answers: A request for God’s exaltation, followed by singing of His power
A description of enemies, followed by a request for forgiveness
A request for life, followed by receiving a crown
medium.explanation: The verse first asks God to be exalted and then promises singing and praise.
medium.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in the verse?

answers: Praise is presented as a shared activity
Only the king will sing alone
No one wants to praise God
challenge.explanation: The plural wording presents praise as a communal response.
challenge.q: What does the plural expression “we will sing and praise” suggest?

answers: Salvation and joy lead to praise for the LORD’s power
Blessings lead to abandoning the LORD
The king’s joy leads to fear
challenge.explanation: The psalm moves from the king’s salvation and joy to praise for God’s power.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the themes at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: So that His power may be recognized and praised
So that the enemies may exalt themselves
So that the king may hide his joy
challenge.explanation: The request leads to singing and praising the LORD’s power.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of asking the LORD to be exalted in His strength?

paragraphs.idea: At the end of the psalm, the poet asks the LORD to be exalted in His strength so that all may sing and praise His power.
